bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where utf-8 encoding failures in malformed .aff files are not properly handled.
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable hunspell revision 74b08bfb8b611b7ae4bea2a6f1f74d9f73c1d0e3, the 36-byte witness is split by `affdicfuzzer` into a 5-byte query word, a 15-byte `.aff` file, and a 15-byte `.dic` file. The `.aff` half is exactly `SET UTF-8\nKEY \xff`, so affix parsing first enables UTF-8 mode and then stores a malformed one-byte KEY token. `SuggestMgr` later converts that KEY string with `u8_u16(ckey_utf, ckey)`. For the single `0xff` byte, `u8_u16()` enters its `0xf0` default case, stores one replacement `w_char` in `ckey_utf`, shrinks the vector to length 1, and returns `-1`. The vulnerable constructor assigns that error return directly to unsigned `size_t ckeyl`, so `ckeyl` becomes a huge value while `ckey_utf` still has one element. During suggestion generation the cleaned witness word reaches the lowercased retry at `HunspellImpl::suggest_internal` line 1051, re-enters `SuggestMgr::suggest`, and takes the UTF-8 `badcharkey_utf` path. Its scan loop trusts `ckeyl` instead of the real vector size and reads `ckey_utf[1]`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/hunspell/suggestmgr.cxx:622`. The fix commit 5aa940a5a3b65263db809953024e9689e191868f records the `u8_u16()` return in a signed temporary and assigns `ckeyl`/`ctryl` only when the conversion did not return `-1`.

source.description: First scored project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input state. When the parser reads the first affix line `SET UTF-8`, this statement stores the attacker-controlled encoding token into `encoding`, creating the state that later enables UTF-8 conversion of the malformed KEY string.
source.value_from: The staged witness is the exact 36-byte file `gt_results/arvo_51102/poc` (sha256 `1ebb88cbdb41116160d1045292a31fa7a958ca50d9b3bcb4d2d82442158b7455`). `affdicfuzzer` interprets byte 0 as `wordlen = 5`, materializes the next 5 bytes as the query word `54 ff ff ff ff`, and splits the remaining 30 bytes evenly into `/tmp/test.aff` and `/tmp/test.dic`. That yields `/tmp/test.aff = "SET UTF-8\nKEY \xff"`, so the first parsed affix line is exactly `SET UTF-8` and the second line is the malformed KEY token `\xff` used later by `SuggestMgr`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The second affix line `KEY \xff` is parsed here and stored as the malformed one-byte keyboard-neighbor string `keystring = "\xff"`. That attacker-controlled KEY token is the value whose failed UTF-8 conversion later corrupts `ckeyl`.

root_cause.description: Unchecked error-to-size conversion. When `u8_u16()` reports UTF-8 conversion failure with `-1`, this constructor stores that signed error value directly into unsigned `size_t ckeyl` instead of rejecting it, leaving `ckeyl` huge while `ckey_utf` contains only the single replacement element produced by the failed conversion.
root_cause.note: The upstream fix changes this call to `int len = u8_u16(ckey_utf, ckey); if (len != -1) { ckeyl = len; }`, and applies the same guard to `ctryl`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `badcharkey_utf()` scans the UTF-16 keyboard-neighbor vector using corrupted `ckeyl` as the bound, so after the first in-bounds comparison it reads `ckey_utf[1]` even though the failed KEY conversion left `ckey_utf` with only one `w_char` element.
sink.note: The saved ASan report says this is a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/hunspell/suggestmgr.cxx:622:29`, and that the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of a 2-byte region allocated in `u8_u16()`.

parser_admitted.description: The harness has already written `/tmp/test.aff` and `/tmp/test.dic` from the saved witness. Constructing `AffixMgr` begins project-side parsing of those attacker-controlled files and admits the malformed affix data into Hunspell's internal state.

fine_trace.note: Harness-only step. The staged 36-byte witness is split into the 5-byte query word `54 ff ff ff ff`, `/tmp/test.aff = "SET UTF-8\nKEY \xff"`, and `/tmp/test.dic = ff ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff ff ff ff ff`.
Source. When the first affix line `SET UTF-8` is read from the split witness file, `parse_string()` stores the attacker-controlled token `UTF-8` into `encoding`.
The parsed encoding token enables `AffixMgr` UTF-8 mode, which later drives both the malformed KEY conversion in `SuggestMgr` and the UTF-8 cleaning/lowercasing path in `HunspellImpl`.
The second affix line `KEY \xff` is parsed and stored as the malformed one-byte keyboard-neighbor string `keystring = "\xff"`.
The newly constructed `HunspellImpl` copies `AffixMgr`'s UTF-8 flag into its own `utf8` field. This cross-object state is what later selects the UTF-8 branches in `cleanword2()` and `mkallsmall2()`.

The suggestion manager imports both vulnerability-relevant affix states: the malformed KEY token into `ckey` and the affix manager's UTF-8 flag into its own `utf8`, which selects the UTF-16 suggestion code paths.
Converting `ckey = "\xff"` hits the `0xf0` default case, writes one replacement `w_char` into `dest` (here `ckey_utf`), shrinks the vector to length 1, and returns `-1`.

Root cause. The constructor stores the `-1` return from step 7 directly into unsigned `size_t ckeyl`, so `ckeyl` becomes a huge bound while `ckey_utf` still contains only the single replacement element from the failed conversion.

On the witness word `T\xff\xff\xff\xff`, `cleanword2()` takes the HunspellImpl UTF-8 branch, converts the leading `T` then stops on the first `0xff`, and leaves `dest_utf` (later `sunicw`) as uppercase `T` plus one replacement code unit without checking the `u8_u16()` failure. `get_captype_utf8()` therefore still returns `INITCAP`.

Because step 9 set `captype` to `INITCAP`, the retry branch copies `scw` into `wspace`, lowercases `sunicw` through `mkallsmall2()`, and re-encodes it into a valid UTF-8 retry string before the second `pSMgr->suggest()` call at the ASan caller line 1051.

The lowercase retry `wspace` from step 10 is valid UTF-8, so this `SuggestMgr::suggest()` call converts it into `word_utf` and a nonnegative `wl`. The line 202 early return is therefore bypassed, which is confirmed by the saved stack continuing to `badcharkey_utf()`.
On that retry call, the UTF-8 keyboard-neighbor phase is reached and `badcharkey_utf()` is invoked with the converted retry buffer `word_utf.data()` and its length `wl`.
Inside the sink function, the current retry character is copied from `candidate_utf[i]` into `tmpc`; the subsequent keyboard-neighbor scan compares this query code unit against entries in `ckey_utf`.

Sink. `ckey_utf` contains exactly one 2-byte `w_char`, but `ckeyl` is huge from step 8, so once the crashing iteration finds `ckey_utf[0] != tmpc` it increments `loc` to 1 and immediately reads `ckey_utf[1]`. That matches ASan's report that line 622 performed a 2-byte read 0 bytes past the 2-byte region allocated by `u8_u16()`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_51102 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `affdicfuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `SuggestMgr::badcharkey_utf` at `src/hunspell/suggestmgr.cxx:622`.

format.name: affdicfuzzer split word/aff/dic blob
format.contract: Exactly the 36-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_51102/poc` (sha256 `1ebb88cbdb41116160d1045292a31fa7a958ca50d9b3bcb4d2d82442158b7455`). Byte 0 is `0x05`, so the next 5 bytes become the query word and the remaining 30 bytes split evenly into a 15-byte `.aff` and a 15-byte `.dic`. The crash-relevant property is that the `.aff` half is exactly `SET UTF-8\nKEY \xff`: the first line enables UTF-8 mode, and the second line makes `u8_u16(ckey_utf, ckey)` return `-1` while leaving `ckey_utf` with one replacement `w_char`. The saved run then reaches the lowercased retry at `HunspellImpl::suggest_internal:1051`, so `badcharkey_utf()` scans that one-element vector with corrupted `ckeyl` and reads index 1.
